Irish dance covers both the social forms: Irish dance covers both the social forms — céilí and set dancing, danced together — and the competitive step dance most familiar abroad. Kizomba came from Angola, growing out of: Kizomba came from Angola, growing out of semba, and took shape alongside Cape Verdean and French Antillean zouk music. It is an African dance with a specific history, frequently marketed abroad as though it were generically 'Latin'.
A slow, grounded walking dance from Ango: A slow, grounded walking dance from Angola, practised here on your own. The step is simple and the difficulty is all in the weight — where it sits and how long it takes to arrive.
Weight, which is the entire technique he: Weight, which is the entire technique here. How long it takes to arrive is the dance, and the change we would measure is inside our noise floor.

Garba is a devotional circle dance of Gu: Garba is a devotional circle dance of Gujarat, in western India, danced during Navratri in honour of the goddess. It is worship as much as it is dance, and the circle around the lamp or image is the point of the form rather than a staging choice.
A circle dance for Navratri, built on cl: A circle dance for Navratri, built on clapping patterns and a turning step that carries you around the centre. It is danced for hours, so it starts gently and it is meant to.

Twerk's immediate lineage runs through N: Twerk's immediate lineage runs through New Orleans bounce, and behind that through West and Central African dances in which isolated hip and glute movement is long-established technique. Reggaeton grew from Panama and Puerto Rico out of reggae en español and dancehall. Both were treated as vulgar while they belonged to Black and Latino communities and as fashionable once they did not.

Control versus momentum. The same moveme: Control versus momentum. The same movement driven from the lower back or thrown with the whole body looks similar and is not the same technique.

Heels is a studio style rather than a co: Heels is a studio style rather than a community dance — it took shape in commercial dance studios, largely in Los Angeles, drawing on jazz, on waacking and on burlesque and cabaret traditions. A studio style danced in heels, drawing: A studio style danced in heels, drawing on jazz, waacking and cabaret. Standing, walking and turning all change in heels, so the first work is not choreography but balance.

Breaking was created by Black and Puerto: Breaking was created by Black and Puerto Rican young people in the Bronx in the early 1970s, as part of the same emerging hip-hop culture as DJing, MCing and writing. Its crews and its named moves have documented originators, and the dance existed for decades before institutions took an interest in it.

Anything inverted or on the floor. Our p: Anything inverted or on the floor. Our pose reading is built for an upright body facing a camera, and most of breaking is neither.

Hula is a Native Hawaiian practice in wh: Hula is a Native Hawaiian practice in which dance, chant (mele), genealogy and spiritual life are one thing. It is taught within a hālau under a kumu hula, and that relationship is the form — not an optional traditional framing around it. Hula was suppressed and nearly severed under missionary and colonial rule, and its survival is the direct result of people who kept teaching it anyway.
Hula is a living cultural and spiritual: Hula is a living cultural and spiritual practice, taught inside a hālau under a kumu hula — that relationship is the form, not a framing around it. We are not going to build lessons for it from general-purpose sources, and we would rather leave this page empty than do that. It is on hold until it can be done in partnership with hula practitioners, and that is a decision rather than a place in a queue.
The Running Man — we have measured 4 ind: The Running Man — we have measured 4 independent teachers doing it, and we still will not grade it: what makes this step right or wrong is the timing of the ball and heel of the foot touching the floor, and toe landmarks are the least reliable points a single phone camera produces. We can show you the step; scoring it would be scoring our own noise.
The Roger Rabbit — reference built from: The Roger Rabbit — reference built from 3 teachers, but they disagree about which way round the step is danced (mirrorConfident:false), so we cannot tell a mirrored performance from a wrong one. Shown, not graded, until more teachers settle it.
The Bounce — three independent teachers: The Bounce — three independent teachers HAVE now been measured, and the step is still not graded, for a reason we only learned by measuring: those teachers agree with each other more closely than our own camera noise. 83% of the tolerance we would grade you against comes from that noise floor rather than from anything they actually disagree about; in the lessons we do grade, that share is 9-28%. The movement itself is detected fine — every dip clears the step's own thresholds. What we cannot honestly do is turn that into a number about you.

Whether you are dancing THIS step at all: Whether you are dancing THIS step at all — we check HOW you do the step, never WHETHER it is the step. Measured, not assumed: a hip-hop Running Man cycle and a hip-hop Bounce cycle were both judged against this reference and came back with zero errors (thigh excursion 16.9deg and 14.8deg, both under the 20deg cap that STEP_TOO_LARGE uses).
